transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-05-20 09:30 UTC | Duration 52m | Attendees: Maya, Samir, Jules (Redwood); Olivia, Marcus, Priya, Diego, Nina, Legal rep (LumenGrid)

[00:00] Maya Chen: Alright folks, thanks for joining. purpose of today is to go through the cutover runbook handoff, confirm canary thresholds, and make sure security signoffs are on track. uh please shout if i talk too fast.
[00:22] Olivia Grant: yeah thanks Maya. high level we want minimal blast radius. timeline hasn't moved — still aiming end of month for pilot->prod, but we need ops to own the gates.
[00:34] Samir Patel: quick intro from my side, i'll walk the telemetry and the gating matrix. note, some of the names in the dashboards are from the staging cluster so you'll see 'redwood-deploy-4' which is fine.
[00:46] Marcus Lee: one ask up front — we need a clear P95 and error-rate threshold that if crossed auto-steps down traffic. what's your recommendation?
[00:58] Samir Patel: recommended starting point: P95 < 420ms, P99 < 950ms, 5xx rate < 0.5% over rolling 5m. canary window 15 minutes with steady-state ramp to 10% traffic. if you prefer A/B, we can do 50/50 for experiments but that complicates fallback.
[01:18] Nina Park: sorry, A/B vs canary — can you spell out the ops differences?
[01:25] Samir Patel: sure. A/B splits more for feature experiments; it requires separate control path and analysis to avoid skew. Canary is progressive traffic shift to the new model/endpoint and has a simpler rollback: route back to previous endpoint. for ops, canary is usually safer for infra rollout.
[01:40] Diego Ramos: so canary with 10/30/60/100 ramp? or you prefer 10/50/100?
[01:45] Samir Patel: we recommend 10% for 15m, then 30% for 30m, then 60% for 30m, final 100% after checks. those durations are adjustable; critical are the gating checks at each step.
[01:58] Priya Singh: gating checks meaning what exactly? where do they live?
[02:03] Samir Patel: Good question. gating checks are a set of scripted queries against the telemetry streams: latency (P50/P95/P99), 5xx rate, average token cost, conversational quality heuristics (we surface low-scoring prompts), and error logs. we push those into your grafana dashboard and an alert if threshold exceeded.
[02:25] Marcus Lee: ah ok — and who triggers rollback? automation or human?
[02:29] Maya Chen: typically we recommend automated rollback for catastrophic failures (e.g., >2% 5xx sustained) and human-in-the-loop for softer regressions like token-quality or small latency drift. we'll document both.
[02:39] Olivia Grant: Priya, do you need anything from Redwood on SOC2 artifacts?
[02:43] Priya Singh: yes, particularly the audit log retention, KMS integration details, and a mapping of controls. we saw a quick doc but need confirmation on whether keys rotate automatically or if we need an external HSM.
[02:57] Samir Patel: Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS; for hosted we offer managed KMS with rotation — sometimes the name in the docs reads 'Redwood Dedicate' or 'Redwood Private'. apologies for text mismatches; we'll send the correct artifact.
[03:13] Unidentified (legal): quick note — contract milestone ties to successful cutover, want to ensure acceptance criteria are explicit.
[03:20] Maya Chen: noted, we'll include explicit acceptance criteria in the runbook and align with contract.
[03:26] [05:00] Samir Patel: walking through the runbook draft (shared as link in chat). Step 1: pre-cutover checklist (backups, model pinning, capacity check). Step 2: staging dry run. Step 3: canary ramp plan. Step 4: validation queries and rollback steps. step 5: post-cutover telemetry retention.
[05:36] Marcus Lee: on model pinning — can we pin to a quantized variant for cost predictability? we saw some token-cost spikes in earlier tests.
[05:44] Samir Patel: yes, pinning to a quantized variant (8-bit quant) is supported. tradeoff is small quality delta; our Optimize module suggested a quant profile that kept ROUGE/quality at 98%. we'll attach that profile.
[06:03] Nina Park: token-cost spike — where is that visible? billing dashboard?
[06:07] Samir Patel: token-level breakdown in the console, plus a per-route cost table that you can export. for the canary we recommend exporting a 1h token breakdown snapshot at each gate.
[06:19] Diego Ramos: about monitoring — can we have synthetic tests hitting the endpoints during canary?
[06:23] Samir Patel: absolutely. we suggest synthetic probes that run representative prompts and assert on response latency and quality embedding similarity. we can provide the probe harness.
[06:34] [10:00] Olivia Grant: question on traffic shaping: if a partial region outage occurs, can we route traffic to a different region automatically?
[10:08] Samir Patel: yes, smart routing can fall back to compatible variants in another region. but note that regional fallbacks can increase token latency due to network hops. we recommend reserving a cross-region backup pool for critical routes.
[10:22] Priya Singh: and is data residency a concern? some prompts touch EU customer data so fallbacks must respect residency rules.
[10:29] Maya Chen: good catch. in the runbook we'll add a routing matrix keyed by route, region, and data residency label. auto-fallback will be disabled for residency-sensitive routes — manual failover only.
[10:41] Marcus Lee: about the canary window metrics — what's the roll-forward decision logic?
[10:45] Samir Patel: decision logic: at end of each gate evaluate 1) P95 delta vs baseline < 15%, 2) 5xx abs < 0.5%, 3) token cost deviation < 20%, 4) no new high-severity regressions from the evaluation set. if any fail, pause and either roll back or hold and investigate.
[10:59] Nina Park: who approves move from 30% to 60%?
[11:02] Maya Chen: ops owner on customer side approves, but we also keep a 15-min observation buffer for the Redwood on-call to declare go/no-go.
[11:12] [15:00] Diego Ramos: can we automate the 'hold and investigate' step in the runbook so it creates a postmortem ticket with telemetry dump?
[15:16] Samir Patel: yes, the runbook includes an automation hook to create a ticket (Jira) and attach a telemetry snapshot (5m rolling). we'll need API tokens and permission to post to your Jira project.
[15:29] Marcus Lee: security question — does Redwood store raw prompt content in logs by default? our policy forbids storing PII in logs unless redacted.
[15:38] Samir Patel: default is ephemeral logs; we can configure redaction at ingestion and only store hashed or tokenized artifacts. for Private deployments you can opt out of any longer-term storage.
[15:49] Priya Singh: great, add that as a line item in the compliance checklist.
[15:53] Maya Chen: will do.
[16:00] [20:00] Samir Patel: demo quick peek at the staging dashboard -- (screen share note) you might notice some transcription mislabels — e.g. 'KV cache' sometimes appears as 'K-V cash' in auto captions; ignore that.
[20:21] Olivia Grant: heh, good to know. on canary errors we saw a pattern where a specific prompt set caused token blowouts. can we add prompt-based regression detection?
[20:32] Samir Patel: yes we include a small eval harness that runs your seed prompt set and reports delta in quality metrics. if a prompt set error rate increases beyond 2x baseline we flag it.
[20:43] Nina Park: is the eval sample size configurable? we'd like 1,000 prompts for a realistic baseline.
[20:48] Samir Patel: yes, we can scale it; just note bigger sample increases analysis time, so we'll run smaller warm checks during early gates and larger batch checks at the 60% gate.
[21:00] [25:00] Maya Chen: legal — any blocking items from contract side?
[25:05] Unidentified (legal): we need the acceptance criteria mapped and a brief addendum on rollback credits in case rollback is required for root-cause in Redwood platform.
[25:15] Maya Chen: we can propose language; will loop in pricing.
[25:20] Marcus Lee: on the dry run — can we do a blackout window for background traffic (quiet window) to lower noise?
[25:27] Jules Tan: yes, we recommend a 2h quiet window in the evening; we will coordinate.
[25:35] Priya Singh: KMS question again — who rotates keys and how are rotations communicated to Redwood?
[25:40] Samir Patel: If you manage keys, you control rotation cadence. we provide a webhook for key-change events; the integration supports PKCS11/HSM flows and cloud KMS.
[25:51] [30:00] Nina Park: what about runbook ownership post-cutover? who is primary on-call?
[30:05] Maya Chen: post-cutover Redwood provides a 2-week hypercare with an on-call engineer aligned to your timezone, then handover to your SRE team. we'll document escalation paths.
[30:18] Diego Ramos: should we plan a knowledge transfer session?
[30:21] Maya Chen: yes, included in runbook timeline — a 90-minute KT plus run-through for the SREs.
[30:31] Marcus Lee: telemetry retention — how long do you keep metrics by default?
[30:35] Samir Patel: default 30 days for detailed metrics and 12 months for aggregated. we can extend retention as an add-on.
[30:44] Priya Singh: need retention extended to 1 year for audit. please include cost estimate.
[30:49] Samir Patel: noted, will add to pricing appendix.
[30:54] [40:00] Samir Patel: quick walkthrough of the rollback commands — essentially a single API call to flip routing back to previous model and an infrastructure script to scale down new pools. we also surface a 'graceful failover' that drains sessions.
[40:15] Diego Ramos: anything about KV cache invalidation? if we rollback we want to ensure stale KV entries don't cause errors.
[40:22] Samir Patel: good point — the runbook includes steps to invalidate prefix caches and warm KV caches on the previous model. we recommend a short warm-up period at 10% traffic after cache flush.
[40:35] Nina Park: are there any known quirks with specific models or quantizations during warm-up?
[40:39] Samir Patel: some 4-bit quantized variants show longer initial latency due to kernel compilation on first few sequences; we recommend preloading models in the pool before traffic ramp.
[40:51] Marcus Lee: ok that's actionable.
[40:54] [45:00] Maya Chen: circling back — summary of owners: Maya will send runbook, Samir leads telemetry and staging shifts, Marcus runs staging, Priya for compliance, Jules schedules dry run. any objections?
[45:16] Olivia Grant: no objections. one ask — include an exec one-pager that maps risk and mitigations for legal and procurement.
[45:25] Maya Chen: will include that.
[45:29] Unidentified (legal): please cc procurement on the KT invites.
[45:33] Maya Chen: noted.
[45:36] [50:00] Maya Chen: last call — confirm dry-run week target 2026-05-29, runbook v1 out by 2026-05-22, staging shift by 2026-05-26. thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with attachments and links.
[50:58] Olivia Grant: thanks all.
[51:05] End of recording.

Notes: few transcription artifacts (mis-labeled product names), some attendees partially identified; shared artifacts referenced: cutover-runbook-v1 (link), canary-dashboard (link), compliance-checklist (link).
